observed.open_side: At server open: newUserClient waitQuietController, then the release (no log), then open(): 'kPEDisableScreen 1' (route was video, index 1; now serial), 'console disabled', enableController 0x0, displaysOnline (online, so open() records gIOFBConsoleFramebuffer = this).
observed.power: The whole console has no '[FB??-A]::setPowerState' line, although IOFramebuffer::setPowerState starts with an unconditional DEBG1 and other DEBG1 lines from the same object print. The framebuffer never received a power-state change; the only setPowerState line is the display wrangler's ('[W]::setPowerState (4)').

mechanism_from_source.design: Patched kernel: the server open path releases (kPEReleaseScreen with NULL, so gc_reacquire_text stays FALSE and gc_acquired becomes FALSE) and then disables (route to serial, last_console=1). Text comes back only through an explicit kPEAcquireScreen from IOFramebuffer::close(). PE_initialize_console then restores the route and initialize_screen(kPEAcquireScreen) runs gc_enable(!graphics_now) with gc_acquired FALSE. kPEAcquireScreen deliberately prints nothing, so the log cannot show whether it ran.
mechanism_from_source.gate: IOFramebuffer::close() (IOFramebuffer.cpp:10341-10347) issues kPEAcquireScreen only if (this == gIOFBConsoleFramebuffer) && getPowerState() && !(timingInfo.flags & kDisplayModeAcceleratorBackedFlag).

condition_results.why: IOGOPFramebuffer does not override getTimingInfoForDisplayMode; the base returns kIOReturnUnsupported, so timingInfo is zeroed (IOFramebuffer.cpp:10710-10716).

open() sets it when updateOnline() is true and it is unset (IOFramebuffer.cpp:9300-9304), and 'displaysOnline' was logged. This is the only framebuffer, and nothing in the log shows suspend or findConsole clearing it.

In every PureDarwin tree here (IOFramebuffer.cpp 1bb98e66 in baseline/bringup/firstboot/desktop/ram-probe), neither IOFramebuffer nor IOGOPFramebuffer calls registerPowerDriver. start() only does PMinit/joinPMtree/temporaryPowerClampOn. With no power states, fCurrentPowerState stays kPowerStateZero and IOService::getPowerState() returns 0 (IOServicePM.cpp:3591-3597). The missing '[FB??-A]::setPowerState' line agrees. In Apple's stack the power driver is registered by the framebuffer subclass; the PureDarwin IOGOP subclass never does.

mechanism_from_source.conclusion: Most likely cause: the stock close() gate requires a power-managed framebuffer, and IOGOPFramebuffer is not power-managed. So kPEAcquireScreen is never issued, the route stays serial, gc_enable stays FALSE, and the last compositor frame remains in the framebuffer. This fits every observation (no pixel change at all, serial output continuing). It is not runtime-proven, because the acquire path has no log.

explicit_unknowns: Whether close() actually skipped kPEAcquireScreen: no log exists on that branch.
Whether gIOFBConsoleFramebuffer was still this framebuffer at close (strongly expected, but not logged).

Whether, if the acquire had run, text would have reached the panel memory unchanged. vinfo still describes the boot framebuffer, which is the same physical memory PDGOP used, as the attempt-002/003 pixels show.
proposal_inputs_for_astra_source_only: Observability first, so the next return run decides it from the log: in PE_initialize_console log 'kPEAcquireScreen %d' (last_console); in IOFramebuffer::close log the three gate values (console==this, getPowerState(), accelerator flag) before the if.

Narrow fix candidate: let close() treat a framebuffer with no registered power driver as powered for this console return only, e.g. through a PureDarwin-local property set by IOGOPFramebuffer that close() checks next to getPowerState(). The other two conditions stay unchanged.

Avoid as a quick fix: registering a real power driver in IOGOPFramebuffer. That puts the framebuffer under the display wrangler's idle/dim policy, and IOFramebuffer::setPowerState(0) carries WindowServer and system-sleep handshakes never exercised on this platform. If it is ever done, it needs its own review and run.
Keep the existing rules: no forced VC acquire while a compositor owns the framebuffer, and console return is qualified only from post-close pixels with the fresh RETURN nonce.
page_probe_note: Recorded as observations only (no verdict): getpagesize/sysconf/host_page_size 16384, vm_page_size 4096 with vm_page_mask 16383 and vm_page_shift 14, vm_kernel_page_* 16384/16383/14. The libSystem vm_page_size global disagrees with its own mask and shift; that is Grok's thread.
